cards.prompt: Put Shimul's readiness steps in a sensible order.
steps: Map every guideline and framework control to an owner and current status
Close or plan each gap, with dates and approval from the right committee
Gather evidence: policies, minutes, risk assessments, audit reports, test results and incident records
Check training records by audience against the joining, 60-day and annual rules
Report readiness to the board and submit compliance plans for any remaining gaps
Keep monitoring KPIs and audit findings after the deadline

items.label: Mean time to detect
items.detail: How fast incidents are spotted after they start.

items.label: Mean time to respond
items.detail: How fast the bank contains and resolves incidents.

items.label: Critical vulnerabilities
items.detail: Whether the number of critical vulnerabilities falls over time.

items.label: Awareness training
items.detail: How often training runs and what share of staff complete it.

cards.question: Which statement about the PDPA 2026's Chief Data Officer duty is accurate as of November 2026?
options: It already applies to every bank in Bangladesh
It is for significant data fiduciaries and starts on a later date the Government will notify
It was removed when the Act was passed
It applies only to foreign banks
cards.explanation: Section 23 requires significant data fiduciaries to appoint Chief Data Officers, but section 1(3) delays that section until a date notified after 18 months.

cards.title: Inside Shimul's readiness report
cards.body:
Farhana's final board paper, two weeks later:

- **Policy:** the ICT Security Policy is board-approved and now maps every framework control to an owner.
- **Governance:** the CISO has an approved team and budget; the ICT Security Committee meets monthly.
- **Risk:** the annual ICT risk assessment is done; three high risks have approved treatment plans.
- **Assurance:** internal and external IS audits are complete; the shared admin account is gone.
- **Incidents:** the ransomware case was reported to BGD-CIRT and Bangladesh Bank inside 72 hours of occurrence; the post-incident review led to new backup isolation.
- **Training:** all 140 overdue joiners finished the email session online; annual awareness reached 97 percent; admins and developers have role training.
- **Data protection:** consent wording and data-sharing rules for partners are being updated for the PDPA.
- **Open items:** two technical controls need until March 2027; a compliance plan goes to Bangladesh Bank.

cards.title: What inspectors usually ask for
cards.body:
- The **board-approved ICT Security Policy** and the date of its last review.
- **Training logs** showing joining dates against awareness and email session dates.
- The latest **ICT risk assessment** and approved treatment plans.
- **IS audit** reports and evidence that findings were closed.
- **Incident register**, reports sent and post-incident reviews.
- **Compliance plans** and any dispensation granted.

Keep the evidence ready; it is much harder to rebuild after the visit is announced.

cards.title: Stage 5 take-aways
items: PDPA 2026: valid consent the bank can prove, no disclosure beyond the purpose without consent, security, retention limits and breach notice.
The CDO duty and the complaint, fine and compensation sections of the PDPA start later; check current notifications.
The Cyber Security Act 2026 creates the Agency and national CERT, lets the Government declare critical infrastructure and punishes cyber offences.
Training must cover every audience: all staff yearly, new joiners within 60 days, managers, privileged users, ICT staff, the CIRT and vendors.
Readiness means evidence: policies, risk assessments, audits, incident records, training logs, KPIs and compliance plans.

cards.prompt: If a Bangladesh Bank inspector asked you tomorrow to show how you met your security training duties, what records could you produce? What will you do this month to make them complete?

quiz.question: Under section 5 of the PDPA 2026, which description of valid consent is correct?
options: Implied whenever a customer opens an account, with no need to explain the purpose
Freely given, specific, clear and withdrawable, after the person is told the purpose, retention, transfers and withdrawal process
Valid only if given in writing before a notary, and then permanent
Required only for sensitive data such as health records
quiz.explanation: Section 5(2) requires consent to be voluntary, specific, clear and revocable, given after the person is informed of the purpose, retention period, transfer and how to withdraw.

quiz.question: Who bears the burden of proving that consent was properly given under the PDPA 2026?
options: The customer who gave consent
The National Data Management Authority
The data fiduciary, such as the bank
The bank's external auditor
quiz.explanation: Section 5(4) places the burden of proving valid consent on the data fiduciary.

quiz.question: From when is the PDPA 2026 deemed to be in force for most of its provisions?
options: 6 November 2025
10 April 2026
31 December 2026
1 January 2028
quiz.explanation: Section 1(3) deems the Act effective from 6 November 2025, except section 23 and sections 31 to 35, which start on a date notified after 18 months.

quiz.question: A bank suffers a personal data breach that is likely to cause significant harm to customers. What does section 20 of the PDPA 2026 require?
options: Notify every affected customer individually within 24 hours by registered post
Notify only Bangladesh Bank, which informs the Authority
Nothing until the Chief Data Officer section is in force
Notify the Authority in the form, manner and time that regulations set
quiz.explanation: Section 20 requires the data fiduciary to inform the Authority of such a breach in the form, manner and time fixed by regulations. The 72-hour framework rule may also apply if it is a critical cyber incident.

quiz.question: Which body is the 'Authority' under the PDPA 2026?
options: The Bangladesh Financial Intelligence Unit
The National Data Management Authority set up under the National Data Management Act 2026
The Bangladesh Telecommunication Regulatory Commission
The National Cyber Security Agency
quiz.explanation: The Act defines the Authority as the National Data Management Authority established under section 8 of the National Data Management Act 2026.

quiz.question: Under section 15 of the Cyber Security Act 2026, who may declare a computer system or network to be critical information infrastructure?
options: The Government, by notification in the official gazette
Bangladesh Bank, by circular to banks
Each bank's board of directors, for the bank's own systems
The courts, after a cyber offence trial
quiz.explanation: The Government may declare critical information infrastructure by gazette notification and must update the list at least once a year.

quiz.question: Someone uses a stolen internet banking login to move a customer's money without lawful authority. Which provision of the Cyber Security Act 2026 deals with this kind of conduct?
options: Section 15, on declaring critical information infrastructure
Section 5, on setting up the National Cyber Security Agency
Section 52, on publishing an English text
Section 24, on e-transactions from a bank or financial institution without lawful authority
quiz.explanation: Section 24 makes it an offence to carry out an e-transaction from a bank, insurer, financial institution or MFS provider through digital means without lawful authority.

quiz.question: 140 joiners passed 60 days without the email security session. Which response best fits the ICT Security Guideline?
options: Record them as trained because induction mentioned email
Apply to Bangladesh Bank for dispensation from the rule
Train them now by e-learning or virtual class, record it and fix the induction process
Wait for the annual awareness campaign next year
quiz.explanation: The guideline lets banks choose delivery methods such as e-learning. Closing the gap quickly, keeping honest records and fixing the process is the right response; false records or delay are not.

quiz.question: Which KPI does the framework suggest for tracking continuous improvement in awareness?
options: Number of security reminder emails sent by the CISO to all staff each month
Total cost of the training institute building
Frequency and completion rates of cybersecurity awareness training
Number of staff who skipped training without penalty
quiz.explanation: Section 7.1.2.4 lists KPIs such as mean time to detect and respond, the trend in critical vulnerabilities, and the frequency and completion rates of awareness training.

quiz.question: When preparing for a Bangladesh Bank ICT inspection, which record best proves the bank met section 6.7.1 of the guideline?
options: A copy of the guideline signed by the CISO
The vendor's brochure for the e-learning platform
A list of staff who hold professional certifications
Training logs that show each employee's joining date and their awareness training dates every year
quiz.explanation: Section 6.7.1 requires awareness training on joining and annually. Records that link joining dates to training dates for each employee show it was done on time.

regulators: National Cyber Security Agency (Cyber Security Act 2026)
National Data Management Authority (Personal Data Protection Act 2026)

references.title: Guideline on ICT Security for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions, Version 4.0 (issued by BRPD Circular No. 10 of 19 June 2023)
references.note: Applies to all Bangladesh Bank-regulated providers; security awareness for all staff on joining and every year; email security session within 60 days of joining; governance roles, annual ICT risk assessment and IS audits; access and privileged-user controls; incident response and CIRT; SWIFT controls; outsourcing.

references.title: Guidelines on Cybersecurity Framework, Version 1.0 (2026)
references.note: Seven functions; qualified CISO; incident roles; awareness and training for all staff, security staff, privileged users, executives and vendors; staff screening; backups and exercises; critical incidents reported to stakeholders incl. BGD-CIRT and Bangladesh Bank within 72 hours of occurrence; yearly cybersecurity audit.

references.title: BRPD-2 Circular No. 02: Cybersecurity Framework, Version 1.0 (2026)
references.note: Issues the framework to banks, finance companies, MFS providers, PSPs, PSOs and other financial service providers; compliance is due by 31 December 2026; queries go to the ICT audit, inspection and compliance wing of Bangladesh Bank's ICT Department.

references.title: BRPD-1 Circular No. 10: Guidelines on Foundation Training for the Newly Recruited Scheduled Bank Officials
references.note: Foundation training for new officers must cover data protection and cyber security.

references.title: Personal Data Protection Act, 2026 (Act No. 63 of 2026)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Deemed in force from 6 November 2025 except section 23 and sections 31-35; consent must be free, specific, clear and withdrawable and the fiduciary must prove it; no disclosure beyond the collection purpose without consent; security measures; retention limits; breach notice to the Authority; Chief Data Officers later.

references.title: Cyber Security Act, 2026 (Act No. 81 of 2026, as amended by Act No. 99 of 2026)
references.issuer: Parliament of Bangladesh (Laws of Bangladesh portal)
references.note: Deemed in force from 21 May 2025; sets up the National Cyber Security Agency, national CERT and SOC; organisations must inform the national CERT of a cyber incident without delay; critical information infrastructure is declared, inspected and audited yearly; unauthorised e-transactions from banks are an offence.

references.title: Code of Conduct for Banks and Non-Bank Financial Institutions
references.note: Requires complete secrecy of customers' affairs and account information and protection of confidential information.

references.title: Bangladesh Bank Annual Report 2015-2016, Chapter 14: Bangladesh Bank's Accounts for 2015-2016
references.note: Records that in February 2016 unauthorised transactions processed by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York paid about USD 81.19 million from Bangladesh Bank's account to third-party accounts at RCBC in the Philippines, and the recovery steps taken.

references.title: Bangladesh Bank-Federal Reserve Bank, New York Joint Statement (1 February 2019)
references.note: Announces a Resolution and Assistance Agreement under which the New York Fed gives technical help in Bangladesh Bank's litigation to recover funds stolen in the 2016 cyber fraud event.

bank.question: A mobile financial service provider regulated by Bangladesh Bank asks whether the 2026 Cybersecurity Framework applies to it. What is the correct answer?
options: Yes. The framework covers banks, financial institutions, MFS providers, PSPs, PSOs and other financial or payment service providers.
No. The framework is limited to scheduled banks listed under the Bank-Company Act.
Only if the provider also operates ATMs or card networks in Bangladesh.
Only from 2027, after the banks have complied first.
bank.explanation: Section 1.1 of the framework names MFS providers among the covered institutions, and BRPD-2 Circular No. 02 was addressed to them as well. All must comply by 31 December 2026.

bank.question: A bank's compliance team lists its ICT security training duties. Which combination correctly reflects the ICT Security Guideline v4.0?
options: Awareness every two years; an email session within 90 days of joining for officers only; management training on governance optional
Awareness on joining and every year; email session within 60 days of joining; management training on ICT governance
Awareness only for IT staff; an email session at the annual general meeting; management briefed by vendors
Awareness on joining only; email training recommended but no time set; management exempt
bank.explanation: Sections 6.7.1, 5.14.9 and 13.1 set these duties. Section 13.3 adds general user awareness and periodic seminars covering all employees.

bank.question: An ICT manager argues that because the 2026 Cybersecurity Framework exists, the 2023 ICT Security Guideline no longer applies. How should the CISO respond?
options: He is right: the framework repealed the guideline from 29 March 2026
He is right only for scheduled banks; NBFIs and MFS providers must still follow the 2023 guideline
Both apply: the framework sits alongside the guideline, so its controls still bind the bank
Neither applies until the bank's board adopts them by resolution
bank.explanation: The framework builds on ISO 27001, national ICT policies and the ICT Security Guideline itself and is meant as a baseline alongside it; nothing in the circular withdraws the guideline.

bank.question: A bank has failed twice to fix a known ICT guideline non-compliance within the time it set itself. Under section 1.3, what should it have done, and what is the risk now?
options: Informed the National Cyber Security Agency, which grants extensions to banks; no penalty of any kind is then possible
Sought dispensation from Bangladesh Bank; after repeated failures a penalty may be imposed depending on the impact
Nothing; the guideline sets minimum standards without any enforcement route
Asked its external auditor to waive the requirement for one more year
bank.explanation: Section 1.3 expects a monitoring team, a time-bound fix and, if the fix fails, a request for dispensation. Multiple compliance failures can lead to a penalty, depending on business or customer impact.

bank.question: Bangladesh Bank's 2015-2016 accounts describe the February 2016 event on its New York Fed account. Which statement matches those accounts?
options: Unauthorised transactions paid about USD 81 million to accounts at RCBC in the Philippines, and RCBC let much of it be paid onward despite instructions to halt
About USD 81 million was stolen from domestic customers' accounts at Bangladeshi banks through fake ATM cards
The New York Fed refused all the payment orders, so no money left the account
The whole amount was returned within a week by the Philippine central bank
bank.explanation: The accounts record unauthorised payments of about USD 81 million into third-party RCBC accounts; RCBC allowed onward payment despite Bangladesh Bank's instructions, and only part was later recovered.

bank.question: In 2019, Bangladesh Bank and the Federal Reserve Bank of New York issued a joint statement about the 2016 cyber fraud. What did it announce?
options: A settlement in which the New York Fed repaid the full amount to Bangladesh Bank
The closure of Bangladesh Bank's account at the New York Fed
A finding that Bangladesh Bank staff had authorised the payments
A Resolution and Assistance Agreement under which the New York Fed gives technical help in Bangladesh Bank's litigation to recover the funds
bank.explanation: The 2019 joint statement describes the agreement for technical assistance in litigation against those complicit in the fraud, including joint meetings with Philippine parties.

bank.question: A new HR officer joined on 2 January and attended general induction on day one. The email security session is planned for 15 March. Is the bank compliant with section 5.14.9?
options: Yes. General induction on day one already satisfies all the email training duties
Yes. The 60-day rule applies only to ICT staff
Yes. The guideline only recommends this session
No. 15 March is more than 60 days after 2 January, so the session is late
bank.explanation: The session must take place within 60 days of enrolment; 2 January plus 60 days is early March. Only the yearly refresher is a recommendation.

bank.question: Which statement about the BRPD-1 Circular No. 10 of 2026 on foundation training is accurate for this topic?
options: Foundation training for newly recruited officers must cover data protection and cyber security
It replaces the ICT guideline's annual awareness duty for all staff
It applies only to newly recruited officers who are placed in ICT, information security and SOC roles
It makes cyber training optional for officers already confirmed
bank.explanation: The 2026 foundation training guidelines require new officers' foundation training to include data protection and cyber security; the guideline's joining and annual awareness duties still apply to all staff.

bank.question: A treasury officer receives an email from the MD's correct-looking address asking her to send this week's dealing positions to a personal Gmail address 'for a board meeting tonight'. What should she do?
options: Send it, because the address looks right and the MD is senior
Send it but password-protect the attachment and text the password to the same address
Not send it; verify with the MD's office by a known channel and report suspected email compromise
Reply to the same email asking the sender to confirm the request in writing, then send the file once the reply arrives
bank.explanation: Confidential data must not go to outsiders by email without approved encryption, and pressure from a senior name is a classic pretext. Verifying through a separate channel and reporting are the safe steps; replying to the same mailbox verifies nothing.

bank.question: Which item is NOT among the end-user phishing defences listed in section 6.7.1 of the ICT Security Guideline?
options: Be suspicious of unexpected email messages or of messages from unknown senders
Forward unexpected emails to colleagues so several people can judge them
Never share sensitive information via email
Avoid clicking links received by email, chat or social networks
bank.explanation: Section 6.7.1 lists suspicion of unexpected messages, never opening unexpected attachments, never sharing sensitive data by email and avoiding links. Forwarding a suspicious message spreads it.

bank.question: A caller claiming to be from Bangladesh Bank's inspection team asks a branch officer for the names of the branch's ICT staff and the brand of its firewall 'to prepare for the visit'. What is the best response?
options: Decline to give the details and refer the caller to head office, which can verify the request through official channels
Give the details, because inspectors have a right to information
Give the staff names but not the firewall brand
Ask for the caller's mobile number and send the details by SMS
bank.explanation: Section 6.7.4 says staff must not reveal information about the organisation, including its structure or networks, unless confident of the person's authority. Official requests can be verified through head office.

bank.question: The help desk receives a ticket from a user's own email account asking to register a new token device because the old one was lost. The user is on leave. What does section 6.7.3 require?
options: Provision it, because the request came from the user's own official bank mailbox
Provision it but limit the token to read-only use for a week
Refuse all token changes while staff are on leave
Verify the user's identity independently before provisioning the new token
bank.explanation: Section 6.7.3 requires identity verification before modifying authentication credentials, including provisioning new tokens. A mailbox may itself be compromised.

bank.question: An officer working from home lets her teenage son use her laptop for school work while it is connected to the bank's VPN. Which rules has she broken?
options: None, because the VPN encrypts everything
Only the rule on switching off computers at the end of each workday
The work-from-home rules: keep bank information from being seen by unauthorised people and do not share access devices or credentials
Only the email disclaimer rule
bank.explanation: Section 5.15 requires staff to stop unauthorised people viewing sensitive information and bars sharing access devices or credentials; a connected bank laptop gives the user access through her credentials.

bank.question: A branch wants to offer account balance enquiries through a chat channel on social media. Which requirement in section 11.9 of the guideline applies?
options: Use any popular platform, provided customers accept the platform's terms and the bank's general account terms
Use only end-to-end encrypted messaging channels and keep monitoring for phishing links and fake accounts
Use a public page so that all customers can see the answers
Use staff members' personal accounts to reply faster
bank.explanation: Section 11.9 requires specific terms and conditions, end-to-end encrypted channels, continuous monitoring for phishing and fake accounts, and fast take-down of malicious content.

bank.question: Which statement best describes what the email security session for new joiners must include under section 5.14.9?
options: How to configure the mail gateway and DKIM records for the bank's domain
How to use a personal email account safely for business whenever the bank's mail system is down
Why detecting phishing matters, email etiquette and how to report incidents inside the bank
How to write the confidentiality disclaimer for each outgoing email
bank.explanation: The guideline lists phishing detection, email etiquette and internal incident reporting as the content of the session, with regular staff communication on email security.

bank.question: A loan officer received a link by SMS, opened it and entered her network password before noticing the URL was wrong. She is embarrassed and wants to just change her password. What is the best advice?
options: Report it immediately so the security team can check for misuse, reset access properly and warn others
Change the password herself and say nothing, since no harm is visible
Wait to see whether anything unusual happens on her accounts over the next week before raising anything formally
Tell only her line manager informally to avoid a formal record
bank.explanation: The guideline requires abnormal activity to be reported immediately. An attacker may already have used the password; a prompt report limits damage and helps others.

bank.question: Which pair of requirements comes from section 5.12 of the ICT Security Guideline on desktops and laptops?
options: USB ports must be open, and users may install approved freeware without asking
USB port access is controlled, and users may not install software without prior authorisation
Laptops need no encryption if kept in the office, and screens lock only at night
Users may disable antivirus during large downloads, provided they report any viruses found each month
bank.explanation: Section 5.12 controls USB access, bans unauthorised software installation, requires encrypting sensitive data on laptops, locking unattended workstations and reporting abnormal activity immediately.

bank.question: The ICT Division proposes accepting the risk of running an unsupported operating system on a branch server for six more months. Under chapter 3 of the guideline, what must happen first?
options: The ICT Division head can accept it alone, because ICT owns the server
The branch manager decides, because the server is in the branch
Nothing; unsupported systems are outside ICT risk management
The risk must go through the formal escalation process to someone with authority to accept it, with any residual risk recorded
bank.explanation: The guideline requires a formal escalation process identifying who may accept a risk, treatment plans approved by the ICT Risk Management Committee and recording of residual risk.

bank.question: Which description of risk appetite and risk tolerance matches section 3.1.3 of the guideline?
options: Appetite is set by the external auditor; tolerance is set by each branch manager
Appetite and tolerance are the same thing and need no approval
Tolerance is the amount of risk accepted; appetite is the IT budget for controls
Appetite is the amount of risk the bank will accept to meet its objectives; tolerance is the acceptable deviation from it, approved by the board or risk committee
bank.explanation: The guideline defines appetite as the risk the bank is prepared to accept and tolerance as tolerable deviation, which needs board or risk committee approval and communication to stakeholders.

bank.question: An IS audit finds that four engineers and a vendor share one privileged account on the payments switch. Which set of fixes best meets section 8.3 of the guideline?
options: Keep the shared account but rotate its password every 30 days
Named privileged accounts limited to need, no account sharing, supervised and monitored vendor access, and timely review of privileged activity
Give the vendor its own permanent administrator account with no monitoring
Disable logging on the switch to improve its performance
bank.explanation: Section 8.3.2 requires strong authentication, restricting and reviewing privileged users, granting access on need, banning shared privileged accounts and supervising vendor access.

bank.question: An internal policy sets a password expiry of 180 days for internal users on a system without MFA. What does the guideline say?
options: It is acceptable, because the guideline leaves password expiry entirely to each bank
It is acceptable if the password has at least eight characters
It is too long: the maximum validity for internal users is a 90-day cycle
It is too short: the guideline sets a one-year cycle
bank.explanation: Section 8.2.8 caps the password validity for internal users at a 90-day cycle, within the bank's policy; without MFA passwords must also have at least eleven characters.

bank.question: Which statement about information system audits under the ICT Security Guideline is correct?
options: Internal IS audits must be at least yearly and risk-based, and a qualified external auditor must also audit IS at least annually
Internal IS audit is optional whenever a qualified external IS audit is done every two years and its findings are tracked to closure
External IS audits replace the need for internal audit to cover ICT
IS audits are only required for banks that operate SWIFT
bank.explanation: Sections 2.4.5 and 2.5.1 require both internal and external information system audits at least once a year, carried out by qualified and certified people.

bank.question: Under the framework's coordination model, which level approves the implementation strategy and takes risk decisions?
options: The implementation and operations level
The business and process level
Senior management
The external auditor
bank.explanation: Section 2.4 places mission priorities with the board, approval of strategy and risk decisions with senior management, profiles and budgets with the business level, and implementation with operations.

bank.question: HR proposes screening staff only once, on hiring. What does section 3.1.8 of the framework expect?
options: Periodic re-screening as well, covering pending proceedings, outside business interests and credit, plus continuous behavioural monitoring
Screening only on hiring, because repeat checks breach privacy
Re-screening only for staff who are promoted to senior management
Screening only for contract staff and vendors
bank.explanation: The framework requires initial screening, periodic screening with a catch-up process, and continuous behavioural monitoring to manage insider threat.

bank.question: A bank plans to outsource its ATM monitoring. Which set of steps fits chapter 12 of the guideline and the framework?
options: Rely on the vendor's ISO certificate and skip the bank's own evaluation
Sign a short purchase order, because monitoring is not a critical service
Transfer all responsibility for incidents to the vendor through the contract
Follow the board-approved outsourcing policy, sign a written agreement setting roles, evaluate the provider's risk and DR, keep a contingency plan and give vendor staff security awareness
bank.explanation: Chapter 12 requires a board-approved outsourcing policy, written agreements, risk-based evaluation, provider DR and contingency plans without weakening controls; framework 2.12(e) adds awareness for vendors.

bank.question: A data exfiltration began at 2:00 am on Monday, was detected at 6:00 pm on Tuesday and was classified critical at 9:00 am on Wednesday. Under the framework, by when must the report to BGD-CIRT and Bangladesh Bank be made?
options: By 6:00 pm on Friday, 72 hours after it was detected
By 2:00 am on Thursday, 72 hours after the incident began
By 9:00 am on Saturday, 72 hours after it was classified as critical
By the end of the following week, after the investigation
bank.explanation: Section 8.1.2.1 runs the 72 hours from the time of occurrence, so late detection leaves less time. Monday 2:00 am plus 72 hours is Thursday 2:00 am.

bank.question: During a critical incident, a journalist calls the CISO asking for details. What does section 2.5 of the framework say?
options: The CISO must answer, as the single point of contact
Any team member may answer if they stick to the facts
Only the Incident Management Leader (the MD or delegate) or someone they designate may deal with the media
The bank must refuse all comment until Bangladesh Bank has published its own public notice about the incident
bank.explanation: The framework reserves media contact to the Cyber Incident Management Leader or a person designated by them. The CISO is the single contact for users, not for the media.

bank.question: A bank's incident procedure tells staff to report cyber incidents only to Bangladesh Bank. Which gap is most important to close?
options: It should send reports to the stock exchange instead of Bangladesh Bank
It should wait for the annual cybersecurity audit before reporting
No gap: Bangladesh Bank forwards reports to every other body
It omits other routes: BGD-CIRT and other stakeholders within 72 hours, the national CERT under the Cyber Security Act, and the PDPA breach notice to the Authority where relevant
bank.explanation: The framework lists BGD-CIRT, Bangladesh Bank, customers and critical service providers; the Cyber Security Act requires informing the national CERT without delay; the PDPA adds breach notice to the Authority.

bank.question: The ransomware gang threatens to leak data unless paid. The board asks what the framework says about paying. Which answer is accurate?
options: The framework warns that paying does not guarantee the data will be returned and stresses backups and a documented ransomware strategy
The framework allows payment if the amount is below the bank's risk appetite
The framework requires payment when no backups exist
The framework is silent on ransomware
bank.explanation: Lessons learned in section 8.1.4 state that paying a ransom does not guarantee return of data, and section 7.1.1.16 requires documented strategies for ransomware and extortion.

bank.question: Which set of recovery practices does section 7.1.1 of the framework expect?
options: Monthly backups kept on the same server, with restore tests every two years
Automated backups at least weekly, an isolated copy of recovery data, quarterly restore tests and annual incident response exercises
Backups only for customer data, tested when a disaster happens
Daily backups stored only with the vendor, with no restore testing
bank.explanation: The framework asks for weekly or more frequent automated backups, an isolated recovery instance, restore testing at least quarterly and incident exercises at least once a year.

bank.question: Which description of the CIRT under the ICT Security Guideline is accurate?
options: It is an external body run by the National Cyber Security Agency for all banks
It responds immediately to cyber incidents, follows preparation, detection and analysis, containment and recovery, and post-incident steps, and reports to Bangladesh Bank CIRT
It meets once a quarter to review closed incidents only
It is the board committee that approves the ICT budget
bank.explanation: Section 6.4 requires the bank to form its own CIRT, follow the four incident response steps, cooperate and report to Bangladesh Bank CIRT and train its members.

bank.question: A SWIFT operator suggests saving the SWIFT application password in a document on the SWIFT server so night staff can log in. What does section 11.8 of the guideline say?
options: Allowed, provided the document has an obscure name and only the night-shift operators know where it is
Allowed if internet access on the server is open for monitoring
Not allowed: passwords must be kept securely and not stored on servers, and sign-on needs MFA
Allowed during holidays when traffic is low
bank.explanation: Section 11.8 bans storing passwords on servers, makes MFA mandatory and also restricts SWIFT traffic outside working hours, internet and USB access.

bank.question: The bank's SWIFT annual attestation is due. Who must carry out the independent assessment under section 11.8 of the guideline?
options: The bank's own SWIFT operators
Bangladesh Bank's inspection department
Any chartered accountancy firm on Bangladesh Bank's list of auditors eligible for banks
A service provider listed in SWIFT's Cyber Security Service Provider directory
bank.explanation: The guideline requires the independent assessment for the annual SWIFT attestation, against SWIFT's controls framework, to be done at least annually by a SWIFT-enlisted provider.

bank.question: Which statement about incident response training is correct under section 6.3.14 of the ICT Security Guideline?
options: Training must match users' assigned roles and include simulated events
Training is needed only for the CISO and the CIRT leader
Training is a single annual lecture for all staff together, with no exercises
Training is optional if the bank uses a managed security provider
bank.explanation: Section 6.3.14 requires role-based incident response training for information system users and simulated events so staff can respond well in a crisis.

bank.question: A customer withdraws her consent to marketing messages but keeps her loan with the bank. Under the PDPA 2026, what follows?
options: The bank must close her loan account at once
The bank may ignore the withdrawal because she is still a customer
The bank must delete all her data, including loan records
The bank stops marketing to her but may keep processing data needed to perform the loan contract, which has its own lawful basis
bank.explanation: Consent must be withdrawable, but section 5(3) allows processing without consent for performing a contract to which the person is a party, within the Act's limits.

bank.question: Which security measures does section 17 of the PDPA 2026 expect a bank to include?
options: Only a written confidentiality clause in every staff member's employment contract
Only a firewall at the internet gateway
Pseudonymisation, encryption, resilience, timely restoration and regular testing
Only storing data inside Bangladesh
bank.explanation: Section 17 requires technical and organisational measures proportionate to volume, sensitivity and harm, including pseudonymisation, encryption, resilience, restoration and regular testing.

bank.question: Which sections of the PDPA 2026 had not yet started in November 2026?
options: Section 5 on consent and section 16 on disclosure, which both wait for the Authority's new regulations
Section 23 on the Chief Data Officer and sections 31 to 35 on complaints, fines and compensation
Section 17 on security and section 20 on breaches
All sections, until the Government publishes an English text
bank.explanation: Section 1(3) deems the Act in force from 6 November 2025 except section 23 and sections 31 to 35, which start on a date notified after 18 months.

bank.question: A bank officer passes customer account statements to a property developer in exchange for referral fees. Which rules does this break?
options: The Code of Conduct's secrecy of customers' affairs and the PDPA bar on disclosure beyond the collection purpose without consent
Only the ICT guideline's email disclaimer rule
None, if the customers are later offered flats at a discount
Only the Cyber Security Act's rule on critical information infrastructure
bank.explanation: Bangladesh Bank's Code of Conduct requires complete secrecy of customers' affairs, and section 16 of the PDPA forbids disclosing personal data for another purpose without consent.

bank.question: If the Government declares a bank's payment system to be critical information infrastructure, what follows under the Cyber Security Act 2026?
options: The bank is exempt from Bangladesh Bank's ICT guideline for that system
The system must be handed over to the National Cyber Security Agency to run
The Director General may monitor and inspect it, and the bank must audit its internal and external infrastructure every year and report to the Council
Nothing changes unless a cyber offence is committed
bank.explanation: Section 16 provides for monitoring and inspection by the Director General and an annual audit report by each declared critical infrastructure to the National Cyber Security Council.

bank.question: Which group is NOT expressly named for training or awareness in section 2.12 of the Cybersecurity Framework?
options: The bank's shareholders
Privileged users and senior executives
Physical security personnel
Third-party vendors and suppliers
bank.explanation: Section 2.12 covers all staff, security staff certifications, privileged users, senior executives, physical and information security personnel, and third parties such as vendors.

bank.question: A bank's readiness report says the framework 'will be complied with during 2027'. What is wrong with this plan?
options: Nothing; the framework allows a one-year grace period after the deadline
BRPD-2 Circular No. 02 requires compliance by 31 December 2026, so remaining gaps need approved compliance plans and, if exceptional, dispensation
The framework must be complied with by 30 June 2026
The bank need not comply until the Cyber Security Act rules are issued
bank.explanation: The circular sets 31 December 2026 as the compliance date. Under the ICT guideline approach, gaps need compliance plans, and dispensation from Bangladesh Bank is only for exceptional cases and a specific period.

bank.question: A Bangladesh Bank inspector asks the training head to prove the bank met the joining, 60-day and annual training duties. Which evidence is strongest?
options: The training calendar for next year
Photographs of a seminar held at head office
The total training budget approved by the board
Per-employee records linking joining dates to awareness, email session and annual refresher dates, with completion rates by audience
bank.explanation: Only records that tie each employee's joining date to training completion show whether the 6.7.1 and 5.14.9 time limits were met. The framework also suggests tracking completion rates as a KPI.
